note: 2026-08-13, SECOND batch, chairman-authorised, PRE-REGISTERED BEFORE ANY RESULT EXISTS. It exists because the first batch produced an ambiguous observation that this council's own rules forbid me to interpret without a control. Across eleven rows at nine distinct instants from 2026-08-03T18:25Z to 2026-08-11T11:30Z, https://uncitral.un.org/en/commission returned byte length 832338 AND sha256 ca87a113c024605cac35... every time. Today's row 2 returned the SAME byte length 832338 and a DIFFERENT sha256, f9712994f5aec4c9a8c5.... Two rival explanations fit that equally: (A) something of constant length on that page changed between 08-11 and 08-13; (B) this host varies its response per request — as pca-cpa.org was shown to do on 2026-08-12, three digests at one byte length in a single run — and the eleven prior digests coincided. Today's batch fetched the URL ONCE and therefore cannot distinguish them. This batch can, and I am firing it rather than choosing the reading I prefer, because on 2026-08-12 the chairman's cardinal failure was over-claiming on exactly this phenomenon.

decision_rules.D1: UNIT: rows 2 and 3 jointly (the same URL, bare, twice in one run). IF both return ok/200 with EQUAL bytes AND EQUAL sha256, then this host did NOT vary its response between two requests in this run, explanation (B) is not supported, and the cross-day digest change observed this morning is attributable to something that differed between the 08-11 and 08-13 fetches rather than to per-response variation. IF the two rows return equal bytes and DIFFERENT sha256, explanation (B) is DEMONSTRATED on this host, the cross-day comparison is VOID as evidence that anything changed, and the eleven prior identical digests become the thing that needs explaining rather than the baseline. decision_rules.D2: UNIT: row 4 (find 'A/80/17'). POSITIVE CONTROL, and it is here because the integrity officer's standing rule requires one before any absence is read as meaningful. 'A/80/17' matched on this page on 08-04, 08-05, 08-06, 08-07 and 08-09. IF it matches again, the page still carries its prior-session content and this morning's find_matched:false on 'A/81/17' is an absence within an intact page.
